parsed.n_justification: The Naches watershed spans significant elevation (352-1977m) and climatic gradients in the Cascade Range. A 12-column design captures: (1) three elevation bands (low <700m, mid 700-1400m, high >1400m) representing rain-dominated, transitional, and snow-dominated zones; (2) four soil texture classes (sandy loam, loam, silt loam, clay loam) common in volcanic/glacial terrain; (3) spatial replication across the watershed extent. This stratified design enables robust quantification of precipitation partitioning drivers while remaining computationally tractable for multi-decadal simulation and ensemble analysis.
requires_capabilities: ELM single-column mode with custom domain/surface data generation
DATM CLMNCEP forcing extraction for 12 custom locations (1980-2018)
Soil texture parameterization (hydraulic conductivity, porosity, field capacity) for 4 texture classes
Elevation-dependent forcing adjustments (temperature lapse rate, precipitation orographic enhancement)
Water table depth output and validation against USGS well observations
Aggregated runoff validation against USGS streamflow (area-weighted column summation)
Water balance closure diagnostics (P = ET + Q + ΔS + recharge)
Multi-year spinup for soil moisture and water table equilibration
Post-processing: partitioning ratios (ET/P, Q/P, R/P), seasonal analysis, elevation/texture sensitivity
assumptions: Single-column framework neglects lateral subsurface flow and surface routing; runoff aggregation approximates watershed discharge
CLMNCEP forcing adequately represents orographic precipitation gradients when adjusted by elevation
Soil texture classes are representative of watershed heterogeneity; actual spatial distribution requires soil survey integration
Satellite phenology (SP mode) is acceptable; crop/irrigation effects are minor in this forested/alpine watershed
Water table depth (ZWT) serves as proxy for recharge validation; direct recharge measurements unavailable
SNOTEL stations provide adequate constraint on snow accumulation/melt despite point-to-grid scale mismatch
Streamflow validation assumes column runoff can be area-weighted to approximate gauge observations (ignoring routing lag)
ET cannot be directly validated but is constrained by water balance closure and energy balance consistency
200-year accelerated spinup achieves quasi-equilibrium for deep soil moisture and groundwater
1980-2018 period captures interannual variability including ENSO, PDO effects on Pacific Northwest hydrology
Perched water tables and shallow bedrock effects are represented by ELM's default parameterizations
Vegetation distribution (PFT) from default surface dataset is reasonable for Cascade mixed conifer/subalpine forests
